A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ReBaPL and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-C. Retained and added material can be reliably matched across versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original ReBaPL classification experiments, ablations, prompt-diversity measurements, and toy simulations.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds posterior-sample ablations, computational timings, and a longer-training control.

M1.justification: Section 3 revises the specified predictor from averaging K samples from the final cycle to averaging C × K samples across all cycles. The sampler, repulsion mechanism, and architectures remain unchanged. Since v1 already discussed collecting samples across cycles, the PDFs do not establish whether implementation changed or the earlier description was corrected.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 11 classification datasets, four ImageNet domain-shift variants, and Gaussian-mixture toy setting. The added Flowers102 sample-count experiment and timing analyses do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1-4 is unchanged, including CLIP, CoOp, CoCoOp, APP, PromptSRC, MaPLe, and MMRL where applicable. The added 15-epoch MaPLe control changes its training budget, rather than introducing a different comparison method.

E3.justification: New protocols vary K from 1 to 5, time probability metrics at batch sizes 2-32, measure inference across 1-4 cycles on four L4 GPUs, and compare MaPLe training for 5 versus 15 epochs. The existing benchmark splits, 16-shot setting, backbone, and accuracy metrics are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 adds sensitivity to posterior samples per cycle. New A.4-A.5 examine metric overhead, inference scaling, and whether longer baseline training explains the gains. Existing repulsion, distance-choice, batch-size, cycle-count, diversity, and toy analyses remain.

E5.justification: New Table 7 specifies that inference latency is averaged over 20 runs. Accuracy reporting over three seeds is retained and reused in the new sample-count table; moving its description to Appendix A does not increase the original run count. No confidence intervals or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1-4 and existing plotted results are unchanged. New results include Flowers102 HM of 84.07 at K=1 and 84.22 at K=5, metric runtimes in Table 6, and inference latencies in Table 7. Appendix A.5 adds MaPLe HM of 82.00 after 15 epochs versus 83.27 after 5 epochs. These are additional condition-specific results, not improved versions of the original benchmark scores.

T1.justification: The unnumbered posterior-predictive definition in Section 3 changes from a final-cycle K-term mixture normalized by 1/K to an all-cycle mixture normalized by 1/(C × K). This is a limited mathematical revision. The numbered equations, probability-metric derivations, and Appendix C otherwise remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: repulsive cyclical SGHMC, representation-based repulsion, a modular Bayesian extension of prompt learning, and improved generalization. The new supplementary evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: V2 argues that gains primarily come from additional cycles rather than larger K, and explains the three-sample ensemble used for Table 1. It also attributes low overhead to cached representations and parallel inference, and uses the longer-training control to argue against extra compute explaining the gains. These interpretations were absent from v1.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-access link, cached-representation details, training-time measurements, and the four-L4 inference configuration. The existing hyperparameters are unchanged in v1 Table 5 versus v2 Table 8. Backbone, hardware, seed, and AdamW burn-in disclosures are relocated from the main text to Appendix A.

R1.justification: The same 48 references and substantive positioning against APP, VaMP, and other prompt-learning approaches are retained. Changed reference back-links reflect pagination rather than added literature or revised novelty claims.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized grammar and terminology edits, updates the byline and affiliations, adds contact information, and moves implementation details into the appendix. Appendix A gains descriptive subheadings and two subsections, while the overall narrative structure remains stable.

P2.justification: V2 adds three compact tables for sample-count accuracy, metric runtime, and inference latency; the existing hyperparameter table becomes Table 8. Figures and tables shift with text reflow, and Table 1's caption explains its existing color coding. The seven existing figures retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reproducibility and assessment through a clearer ensemble specification, a code-access pointer, sampling sensitivity results, and computational-cost controls. These address practical ambiguities without changing the main benchmark evidence. The gains are limited: latency evidence uses four GPUs, and the new Flowers102 K=1 result in Table 5 (84.07 HM) is not reconciled with Table 1 (84.35 HM) through an explanation of differing settings.
